repairs.before: Strongest feature: Law reconstructs the free-will defense with reversed moral polarity: an evil God needs uncoerced creatures for genuine moral evil and therefore tolerates freely chosen goodness as its price, closely matching the structure used to excuse evil under a good God. Principal limitation: structural mirroring shows that the defense alone does not discriminate, but it does not establish that freedom has identical value, feasibility, or expected distribution for opposed deities, nor does it directly address natural suffering or Ward’s nonomnipotent theology. Live burden: Law must defend the relevant symmetry and integrate free choice with the independent evidence from disease, starvation, and cosmic destruction. Locked score: 86 rewards highly coherent, precise, responsive, and evidentially focused pressure on a standard defense, with limited deductions because analogical parity remains argued rather than comprehensively demonstrated.
repairs.after: Strongest feature: Law reverses the free-will defense: an evil God needs uncoerced creatures to produce moral evil and therefore tolerates freely chosen goodness as its price, preserving the defense’s structure and exposing its failure to discriminate between rival deities. Principal limitation: Structural mirroring does not establish equal value, feasibility, or expected distributions of freedom under opposed deities, and it neither covers natural suffering nor fully accommodates Ward’s nonomnipotent theology. Live burden: Law must defend those symmetry assumptions and integrate free choice with independent evidence from disease, starvation, and cosmic destruction, showing why their distribution favors neither hypothesis. Locked score: 86 rewards the argument’s exceptional coherence, precision, responsiveness, and evidential focus while retaining deductions because analogical parity remains asserted more broadly than demonstrated and important asymmetries remain incompletely tested.
repairs.rationale: Compresses the critique into the required 105–130-word range while preserving the four mandated sentence labels, source-specific symmetry analysis, limitations, live burden, and locked score of 86; the revised text remains above the 880-character minimum.
